title: Metroid Ravenous Revealed for Switch 2 — Samus Embraces Her Metroid Powers in a Darker Follow-Up to Dread
description: Nintendo has revealed Metroid Ravenous for Nintendo Switch 2, launching January 28, 2027. We break down Samus’ new energy-absorbing abilities, combat, enemies, story clues and everything shown in the first trailer.
body:
Nintendo has officially revealed **Metroid Ravenous**, a new 2D Metroid adventure coming exclusively to **Nintendo Switch 2 on January 28, 2027**.

The first trailer immediately positions Ravenous as an evolution of the fast, cinematic 2D design established by **Metroid Dread**, but it also makes one major idea impossible to ignore: the Metroid power inside Samus is no longer just a piece of backstory. It appears to be becoming part of how she survives.

Nintendo’s footage shows Samus moving with the same speed and precision that defined Dread while introducing new enemy encounters, more elaborate close-range action and a striking ability that lets her apparently **absorb energy directly from enemies**. Nintendo’s own marketing language frames the game around an “eat or be eaten” idea, which gives the title *Ravenous* an unusually literal edge.

For a reveal that lasts only a few minutes, there is a lot to unpack — from Samus speaking during the trailer to huge new creatures, mysterious humanoid opponents and several combat sequences that do not look like anything in Dread.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Samus Aran appears during the Metroid Ravenous reveal shown in Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026.

contentBlocks.text: Nintendo confirmed that **Metroid Ravenous launches January 28, 2027** for **Nintendo Switch 2**. The short gap between reveal and release is notable: rather than announcing another distant project, Nintendo is putting the new 2D Metroid in players’ hands in just a few months. That also means the first trailer is likely only the beginning of a rapid information cycle covering the setting, abilities, progression and story before launch.
contentBlocks.heading: Metroid Ravenous launches January 28, 2027

contentBlocks.text: The ending of **Metroid Dread** fundamentally changed Samus, bringing the Metroid DNA inside her to the surface in a dramatic new form. Ravenous appears ready to build an entire game around the consequences instead of treating that transformation as a one-off finale. The title itself now carries obvious thematic weight: hunger, predation and survival are all reflected in the way Samus interacts with enemies in the reveal footage.
contentBlocks.heading: Samus’ Metroid transformation is no longer being treated as an ending

contentBlocks.text: The clearest new mechanic shown in the trailer is Samus apparently **absorbing energy directly from enemies**. Nintendo has not yet explained the exact rules behind the system, so it is too early to say whether it replaces traditional health recovery, fuels special abilities or works as a separate resource. What is clear is that the mechanic is being presented as a central part of Ravenous’ identity rather than a minor contextual action.
contentBlocks.heading: The new energy-absorption mechanic could define Ravenous

contentBlocks.text: One of the strangest sequences in the trailer shows **multiple glowing silhouettes of Samus appearing around an enemy at once**. The effect could represent an evasive maneuver, a rapid repositioning ability, an attack visualization or another mechanic Nintendo has not yet named. It does not read like an ordinary jump, and it appears visually distinct from the familiar movement language of Dread. Until Nintendo explains it, the safest conclusion is simply that Ravenous is adding at least one major new mobility or combat interaction to Samus’ toolkit.
contentBlocks.caption: Multiple glowing images of Samus appear around an enemy during one of Metroid Ravenous’ unexplained new gameplay sequences.
contentBlocks.heading: Samus may have a new high-speed movement or combat ability
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Several glowing silhouettes of Samus Aran surround an enemy during Metroid Ravenous gameplay.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Nintendo / Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026

contentBlocks.text: The underlying movement looks immediately familiar. Samus still transitions quickly between traversal and combat, and the trailer retains recognizable mechanics including the **Morph Ball** and close-range counters. But the emphasis is different. Dread often framed Samus as someone being hunted, particularly around the E.M.M.I.; Ravenous repeatedly frames her as the dangerous presence in the room. The animation, enemy absorption and more physical combat sequences all reinforce that shift.
contentBlocks.heading: Ravenous still moves like Metroid Dread — only more aggressive

contentBlocks.text: One gameplay sequence pits Samus against an enormous segmented creature that nearly fills the screen inside a confined cavern. Nintendo has not identified the encounter as a boss, so it is better not to label it one yet, but the scale is significant. Ravenous appears interested in using Switch 2 hardware for larger creatures and more elaborate cinematic staging without abandoning the side-scrolling structure of modern 2D Metroid.
contentBlocks.caption: Samus faces an enormous segmented creature inside one of Metroid Ravenous’ cavernous environments.
contentBlocks.heading: Ravenous is throwing much larger threats at Samus
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Samus Aran fights a gigantic segmented creature inside a cavern in Metroid Ravenous.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Nintendo / Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026

contentBlocks.text: The reveal also introduces a group of organized humanoid opponents whose presentation immediately separates them from the wildlife Samus usually encounters. Coverage of the trailer has highlighted futuristic caped fighters using blades and unusual spinning weapons. Nintendo has not explained who they are, whether they are connected to Chozo history or what role they play in the attack that sets the story in motion. Their deliberate, coordinated appearance makes them one of the biggest story mysteries coming out of the reveal.
contentBlocks.heading: The mysterious caped fighters may be just as important as the monsters

contentBlocks.text: Samus has spoken before — including a brief but memorable moment in Dread — but Ravenous’ trailer has already drawn attention because her voiced dialogue is presented more naturally inside the story. That does not necessarily mean Nintendo is turning Metroid into a dialogue-heavy game. It may instead signal a middle ground where Samus remains restrained and isolated while responding more directly to the events around her, which would fit a story centered on changes happening to her own body and abilities.
contentBlocks.heading: Samus speaks — and Ravenous may give her a more active role in the story

contentBlocks.text: Everything shown so far makes Ravenous look closely connected to the events and mechanics of Dread, and fans are already calling it **Metroid 6** or **Dread 2**. Nintendo has not formally used either name in the announcement, so Neural Critic is treating those labels as fan shorthand rather than official chronology. The visible continuation of Samus’ Metroid powers nevertheless makes a post-Dread connection difficult to ignore.
contentBlocks.heading: Is Metroid Ravenous effectively Metroid 6?

contentBlocks.text: The name **Metroid Ravenous** first surfaced publicly in July through a Brazilian age-rating listing that appeared before Nintendo had announced the project. The listing identified Nintendo of America and Switch 2, but it did not provide the context the first trailer finally gives us. Today’s Direct confirms that the title itself was genuine; the more interesting story now is what Nintendo has actually built around it.
contentBlocks.heading: The July Metroid Ravenous ratings leak was real

contentBlocks.text: The obvious comparison is **MercurySteam**, the studio behind Metroid: Samus Returns and Metroid Dread, because Ravenous visibly builds on the style of those games. However, Nintendo has not yet detailed the development credits in the material available at the time of publication. Until it does, the developer should remain listed as unconfirmed rather than assumed.
contentBlocks.heading: Nintendo has not yet confirmed Ravenous’ developer

contentBlocks.text: For years, being a Metroid fan often meant long waits between major releases. The modern run has changed that dramatically, with **Metroid Dread**, **Metroid Prime Remastered**, **Metroid Prime 4: Beyond** and now Ravenous keeping the series visible across both its 2D and first-person branches. Ravenous does not look like a side project either; Nintendo is positioning another Samus-led adventure as a major Switch 2 release only months away.
contentBlocks.heading: Metroid is suddenly one of Nintendo’s busiest major series

quickRead: Metroid Ravenous launches January 28, 2027 for Nintendo Switch 2.
The reveal centers on Samus’ evolving Metroid powers and a new enemy-energy absorption mechanic.
The trailer also shows a mysterious multi-Samus movement effect, enormous creatures and organized humanoid fighters.
Nintendo has not yet formally identified the developer in the announcement materials.
conclusion: Metroid Dread ended by transforming Samus. **Metroid Ravenous appears ready to deal with the consequences.** That alone makes this reveal more interesting than a straightforward sequel announcement. The new energy-absorption mechanic, the game’s predatory language and the enemies shown in the first trailer all suggest Nintendo is turning Samus’ Metroid DNA into the defining idea of the next 2D adventure. The biggest questions now are who attacked her, what the new abilities actually cost or consume, who the mysterious fighters are and how far the game is willing to push the transformation that Dread began. We will find out when Metroid Ravenous launches for Nintendo Switch 2 on January 28, 2027.
conclusionHeading: The biggest mystery is not where Samus is going — it is what she is becoming
